answer: I would anchor trust in EigenTrust-style global reputation from peer scores. With reputation computed from who trusts whom, a single jetty check quietly prices out anyone trying to run a hundred names at once. What makes this stick is that reputation computed from who trusts whom cannot be faked in bulk — each proof is independent, and the gale of independence is that one compromised proof endangers no other account. Running a hundred clones would mean a hundred separate proofs, each costing real money and real time, and the orchard of that bill is larger than anything one epoch pays out.
